text:
Maya D: heads-up — we spent a chunk of the sprint retro debating how to attribute cross-tenant inference cost when traces span shared routing layers. want to capture the tradeoffs and land on a pragmatic heuristic.

Ali K: +1. can you summarize the problem we ran into?

Maya D: tl;dr: when a request from tenant A hits the shared gateway, gets routed to a model pool that batches with tenant B, our current billing key (tenant_id) is at the root, but cost per-token is split by host-level batching. billing pipeline ends up double-counting or mis-assigning tails.

Samir P: gist: batch-level CPU/GPU time -> attributed to batch owner (gateway node) today, but product expects per-tenant split. high-cardinality split at aggregation time is expensive.

Jen L: downside of doing exact split: we add per-token lineage events and join at aggregation. that increases cardinality *and* query latency.

Ali K: can we approximate with heuristics? e.g., proportional split by token-count per-tenant in the batch, recorded as lightweight attributes on the batch summary.

Maya D: prototype idea: gateway emits a batch_summary event with fields: ```{
  "node_id": "gw-3",
  "batch_id": "b-2026-04-15-xyz",
  "tenant_token_counts": [{"tenant_id":"A","tokens":120},{"tenant_id":"B","tokens":30}],
  "total_gpu_ms": 48
}``` aggregation multiplies fraction by total_gpu_ms to get per-tenant GPU-ms. lightweight and bounded.

Samir P: +1 on boundedness. concerns: ordering and late-arriving summaries (gateway crash or retry) will distort numbers. how do we make it idempotent?

Maya D: include batch_id + checksum + dedupe TTL at ingest. ingest pipeline keeps only first summary per batch_id. we already dedupe similar for request-logs.

Jen L: ok but product asked for region-aware splits (some batches span regions due to failover). add region tag to batch_summary so we can backfill region splits separately.

Ali K: also need a fallback for samples where tenant_token_counts are missing (older clients). fallback rule: attribute by request-count ratio in the same time window for that tenant on that node. documented and tolerant.

Samir P: meter-level vs offline accounting: we should keep batch_summary for real-time dashboards, and emit detailed lineage only on-demand for audits. keeps normal query volumes low.

Maya D: action items: 1) spec batch_summary schema + dedupe semantics, 2) implement ingest dedupe and TTL, 3) add backfill pipeline for audit-level lineage, 4) docs and SDK helper to emit tenant_token_counts.

Ali K: can we add a small envelope example to the RFC? e.g.: ```{
  "envelope_type":"batch_summary",
  "attrs":{
    "batch_id":"b-...",
    "node_id":"gw-3",
    "region":"us-west-2",
    "total_gpu_ms":"48",
    "tenant_token_counts":"A:120,B:30"
  }
}```

Jen L: looks good. I'll add a section on query examples for cost dashboards (group by tenant, region, with a sum of prorated GPU-ms).

obsv-bot: deploy-bot: new schema draft pushed to //git.redwood/infr/obs/batch_summary_rfc.md — please review.

Samir P: timeline: propose we land the ingest dedupe in this sprint (small infra change), schema and SDK next sprint, backfill / audit pipeline in 2-3 sprints. ok?

Maya D: sounds reasonable. calling out open questions: how to handle model-variant pinning (if a tenant pins a model pool exclusively, we should not prorate). need rule: if batch has a single-tenant pin flag -> attribute 100% to that tenant and mark as "exclusive":true.

Ali K: also ask finance: do they accept prorated GPU-ms as final or do they need a nightly reconciliation job? I'll ping them after this thread.

Jen L: I'll draft the RFC follow-up today and drop a short PR for the schema.

Maya D: awesome. tagging @Ali K @Jen L for reviews. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
